subject.title: [Slack] Agent lacks visibility into own channel messages from DM sessions

question: Should Slack DM sessions receive a scoped self-activity recall surface for the agent’s own channel messages, and what authorization and retention boundaries should govern it?
rationale: The requested capability crosses deliberately separated session boundaries and can reveal channel context in DMs; code alone cannot choose the intended privacy model.

options.title: Approve scoped self-activity recall
options.body: Define an agent-owned outbound activity ledger or read-only recall API with workspace, destination, authorization, and retention limits.

options.title: Keep sessions isolated
options.body: Retain the current boundary and document that agents cannot recall channel activity from unrelated DM sessions.

options.title: Sponsor a broader session model
options.body: Treat this as part of a larger cross-session-memory product design rather than a Slack-specific recall feature.

recommendation.title: Approve scoped self-activity recall
recommendation.body: Define an agent-owned outbound activity ledger or read-only recall API with workspace, destination, authorization, and retention limits.

likelyOwner.reason: The issue’s latest maintainer-facing review and the relevant Slack routing/outbound history both point to this area.
